title: The Excise-Fiscal Diagnostic
subtitle: Reading an excise system against its externalities
message: A light, repeatable report maps any excise schedule onto 30 standard lines, scales each rate three ways and sets fuel rates against one fixed set of damage values. In a stylized country petrol is taxed about right and diesel at less than half its corrective rate.

problem.text: Schedules grow by amendment for decades, in mixed units and currencies, and specific rates erode with inflation. Few ministries can say whether a fuel, tobacco or alcohol tax is high or low against the damage the good does.

mechanism.title: Diesel's gap is mostly air pollution
mechanism.caption: Country A (stylized): US$ per liter; whiskers span the low and high cases.
points: Corrective rate: carbon and air pollution, plus half of congestion, accidents and road damage.
Diesel: $0.18 against $0.43; closing the gap raises about 1.1% of GDP.
AI drafts each stage; every line is checked against the gazetted text.

action.title: Run it every budget cycle
results: Diesel is undertaxed in every case.
Petrol, tobacco and beer share one problem: no indexation.
Spirits pay 44% less per liter of alcohol than beer.
